overview.headline: Constant velocity flight and how range is found from speed and time

keyPoints.point: Students learn that constant speed level flight requires lift equal to weight and thrust equal to drag.
keyPoints.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that ground speed stays constant when wind speed stays constant.
keyPoints.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that distance flown equals ground speed times time aloft.
keyPoints.quote: Our general rate equation then becomes a distance equation: the distance flown is equal to the ground speed times the time aloft.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that maximum range equals ground speed times maximum time.
keyPoints.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

keyPoints.point: Students learn that combat radius is half the range for a round trip mission.
keyPoints.quote: The combat radius would be half of the range as specified here.
